short: Modular on-chain governance framework based on OpenZeppelin's Governor contracts
introduction: OpenZeppelin Governor is a modular on-chain governance framework used by many DAOs and protocols to manage decentralized decision-making. It implements a proposal lifecycle that includes creation, voting, queuing via a timelock, and execution. The system is designed to be highly composable, with interchangeable modules for voting strategies, quorum calculations, and timelock controllers.
designPurpose: OZ Governor was designed to provide a battle-tested, secure governance implementation that protocols can customize without building from scratch. The modular architecture separates concerns like vote counting, proposal thresholds, and execution delays into distinct contracts. Integration with ERC-20 or ERC-721 voting tokens enables token-weighted governance with snapshot-based vote accounting.
commonUsage: DAOs use Governor to manage protocol upgrades, treasury allocations, and parameter changes through community proposals and votes. Token holders delegate their voting power and participate in governance by casting votes on active proposals. The timelock ensures a delay between approval and execution, giving the community time to react to potentially harmful proposals.
fn.propose.desc: Creates a new governance proposal with one or more actions to execute if the vote succeeds. The proposer must hold tokens above the proposal threshold.
fn.propose.params.targets: An array of target contract addresses for each action in the proposal.
fn.propose.params.values: An array of ETH values to send with each action call.
fn.propose.params.calldatas: An array of encoded function calls to execute on each target.
fn.propose.params.description: A human-readable description of the proposal.
fn.propose.returns.proposalId: The unique identifier for the created proposal.
fn.castVote.desc: Casts a vote on an active proposal. The voter's weight is determined by their token balance at the proposal's snapshot block.
fn.castVote.params.proposalId: The ID of the proposal to vote on.
fn.castVote.params.support: The vote type: 0 = Against, 1 = For, 2 = Abstain.
fn.castVote.returns.weight: The voting weight applied to this vote.
fn.castVoteWithReason.desc: Casts a vote on an active proposal with an on-chain reason string, providing transparency for the voting rationale.
fn.castVoteWithReason.params.proposalId: The ID of the proposal to vote on.
fn.castVoteWithReason.params.support: The vote type: 0 = Against, 1 = For, 2 = Abstain.
fn.castVoteWithReason.params.reason: A text string explaining the reason for the vote.
fn.castVoteWithReason.returns.weight: The voting weight applied to this vote.
fn.queue.desc: Queues a succeeded proposal in the timelock for execution after the required delay period.
fn.queue.params.targets: The target contract addresses matching the original proposal.
fn.queue.params.values: The ETH values matching the original proposal.
fn.queue.params.calldatas: The encoded function calls matching the original proposal.
fn.queue.params.descriptionHash: The keccak256 hash of the proposal description.
fn.queue.returns.proposalId: The proposal ID that was queued.
fn.execute.desc: Executes a queued proposal after the timelock delay has elapsed, calling each target with its specified calldata and value.
fn.execute.params.targets: The target contract addresses matching the original proposal.
fn.execute.params.values: The ETH values matching the original proposal.
fn.execute.params.calldatas: The encoded function calls matching the original proposal.
fn.execute.params.descriptionHash: The keccak256 hash of the proposal description.
fn.execute.returns.proposalId: The proposal ID that was executed.
fn.cancel.desc: Cancels a proposal that has not yet been executed. Can be called by the proposer or by governance if the proposer's token balance drops below the threshold.
fn.cancel.params.targets: The target contract addresses matching the original proposal.
fn.cancel.params.values: The ETH values matching the original proposal.
fn.cancel.params.calldatas: The encoded function calls matching the original proposal.
fn.cancel.params.descriptionHash: The keccak256 hash of the proposal description.
fn.cancel.returns.proposalId: The proposal ID that was cancelled.
fn.state.desc: Returns the current state of a proposal: Pending, Active, Canceled, Defeated, Succeeded, Queued, Expired, or Executed.
fn.state.params.proposalId: The ID of the proposal to query.
fn.state.returns.state: The proposal state as a uint8 enum value.
fn.getVotes.desc: Returns the voting power of an account at a specific block number, based on token delegation snapshots.
fn.getVotes.params.account: The address to query voting power for.
fn.getVotes.params.blockNumber: The block number at which to check the voting power snapshot.
fn.getVotes.returns.votes: The number of votes the account held at the given block.
fn.proposalThreshold.desc: Returns the minimum number of votes an account must have to create a proposal.
fn.proposalThreshold.returns.threshold: The proposal threshold in token units.
fn.ProposalCreated.desc: Emitted when a new proposal is created, containing all the details needed to track and vote on it.
fn.ProposalCreated.params.proposalId: The unique identifier of the new proposal.
fn.ProposalCreated.params.proposer: The address that created the proposal.
fn.ProposalCreated.params.voteStart: The block number when voting begins.
fn.ProposalCreated.params.voteEnd: The block number when voting ends.
fn.VoteCast.desc: Emitted when a vote is cast on a proposal, recording the voter, their choice, weight, and optional reason.
fn.VoteCast.params.voter: The address that cast the vote.
fn.VoteCast.params.proposalId: The ID of the proposal voted on.
fn.VoteCast.params.support: The vote direction: 0 = Against, 1 = For, 2 = Abstain.
fn.VoteCast.params.reason: The optional reason string provided with the vote.
sim.full-governance-lifecycle.name: Full Governance Lifecycle
sim.full-governance-lifecycle.desc: Simulates the complete governance flow from proposal creation through voting, queuing in the timelock, and final execution.
sim.full-governance-lifecycle.step.propo: The proposer creates a new proposal by calling propose(). The Governor checks that the proposer meets the proposal threshold via the governance token.
sim.full-governance-lifecycle.step.vote: Voters cast their votes during the voting period. Voter A (500 GOV) and Voter B (300 GOV) both vote For, reaching quorum and passing the proposal.
sim.full-governance-lifecycle.step.queue: The succeeded proposal is queued in the Timelock Controller, which enforces a mandatory delay before execution.
sim.full-governance-lifecycle.step.execu: After the timelock delay elapses, anyone can call execute() to dispatch the proposal's actions to the target contract.
sim.proposal-execution.name: Proposal Execution
sim.proposal-execution.desc: Simulates the execution phase of a queued proposal, showing how the timelock dispatches actions to the target contract.
sim.proposal-execution.step.checkState: Query the proposal state to confirm it is in the Queued state and the timelock delay has elapsed.
sim.proposal-execution.step.callExecute: A caller invokes execute() on the Governor, which forwards the execution request to the Timelock Controller.
sim.proposal-execution.step.dispatch: The Timelock Controller dispatches the call to the target contract, executing the proposal's encoded action. The proposal state becomes Executed.
compose.erc20.role: Voting power typically comes from an ERC-20 governance token using the ERC20Votes checkpoint extension, read by Governor through the IVotes/IERC5805 interface.
compose.erc721.role: ERC721Votes lets NFT collections serve as the voting asset — the only alternative voting-power source shipped in OpenZeppelin Contracts.
compose.erc712.role: castVoteBySig accepts ballots signed as EIP-712 typed data (BALLOT_TYPEHASH), including ERC-1271 contract signatures, enabling gasless voting.
